# Jubilees Chapter 22 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham Blesses Jacob; Abraham's Death

---

**22:1** It came to pass in the first year of the first week of the forty-third jubilee that Abraham returned and dwelt opposite Hebron, at Mamre.

**22:2** Isaac slaughtered a peace offering and brought it to his father Abraham, and Abraham ate. Isaac's wife also brought gifts, and Ishmael's wife brought gifts, and they ate together. Abraham rejoiced, because Isaac had slaughtered a peace offering.

**22:3** In those days Isaac slaughtered a peace offering to the LORD, and at the Feast of First-Fruits of the harvest he sent to his father Abraham some of the first-fruits of all the produce of the field and of the firstlings.

**22:4** Abraham rejoiced greatly and blessed the Most High God who had created heaven and earth, who had made all the fat things of the earth and given them to the sons of men, that they might eat and drink and bless their Creator.

**22:5** "And now I give thanks to you, my God, because you have shown me this day. Behold, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, and I am old and full of days, and all the days of my life have been peace to me."

**22:6** "I was separated from the nations and from the impurity of the Gentiles, and I dwelt among them — but I did not walk in the error of the nations, and I did not go after them or after their abominations."

**22:7** "And you, the living God — you know that the desires of my heart were to do your will, to walk uprightly, and that I turned neither to the right hand nor to the left throughout all my days."

**22:8** Abraham called Jacob and said: "Come, my son — come near, that I may kiss you, my beloved son."

**22:9** Jacob drew near and Abraham kissed him and said: "My son, my beloved — nothing in all this world rejoices my heart as much as you do. May the LORD bless you always, and may you be blessed above all the seed of mankind, for you are the Lord and Light of the nations; you are the son of Abraham, who was counted righteous before the LORD."

**22:10** "For in you and in your seed shall Abraham rejoice before him and be named a prince and blessed before the LORD. Now I command you, my son: observe the commandments of Abraham your father. Keep his righteousness and his ways."

**22:11** "Do not associate with the nations, and do not eat with them, and do not act as they do, and do not become their companion, for their works are unclean and all their ways are a source of abomination and impurity."

**22:12** "They offer their sacrifices to the dead and worship demons, and they eat over graves, and all their works are vanity and nothingness."

**22:13** "They have no heart to understand, and their eyes do not see what their deeds are, and how they err in saying to a piece of wood, 'You are my god,' and to a stone, 'You are my lord and my deliverer' — for these have no heart."

**22:14** "And you, my son Jacob — may God Most High help you, and may the God of heaven bless you and remove you from their impurity and from all their error."

**22:15** "Take care, my son Jacob, that you do not take a wife from any of the daughters of Canaan, for all his seed is to be rooted out of the earth. For when Ham sinned, Canaan also sinned, and his seed is destined for destruction and to be rooted out of the earth; all who remain of him shall be scattered across the earth."

**22:16** "For on account of the transgression of Ham, Noah cursed Canaan, and all his seed is being rooted out of the earth. Because of the impurity of his deeds, he went astray and will be plucked up by the roots."

**22:17** "And now I give you all my commands, my son — keep them. Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan, but take a wife for yourself from my own family — a wife worthy of my son."

**22:18** "May the LORD God of Abraham bless you and bless your seed, and sanctify you as a holy nation, after the likeness of his own will, so that you may keep his law and his righteousness. And may he be your Father, and may you be his firstborn son and people for all time."

**22:19** "Go in peace, my son. May the Most High God — my God and your God — strengthen you to do his will and bless all your seed and the remnant of my seed, throughout the generations of the earth, forever, with the blessing with which he has blessed me."

**22:20** Abraham finished blessing Jacob and then lay down on his bed and was gathered to his fathers.

**22:21** Jacob stood before his father Isaac after the death of Abraham. And Isaac loved Jacob.

**22:22** In those days Isaac and Ishmael came from the well of the oath and dwelt with Abraham during the days of the feast. And Ishmael came with his four sons and his six sons who were then alive, and they all came together.

**22:23** Abraham's servants, Isaac's servants, and Ishmael's servants came and buried Abraham — in the double cave near Sarah his wife, in the field of Ephron the Hittite facing Mamre, the field Abraham had purchased from the sons of Heth.

**22:24** All the sons of his household mourned for Abraham forty days — Isaac and Ishmael and all their sons, and all the sons of Keturah in their places — and the weeping for Abraham was great.

---
*LOGOS notes: The Feast of First-Fruits = Shavuot; central to Jubilees' 364-day calendar and covenant renewal theology. Abraham's blessing of Jacob in chapter 22 is unique to Jubilees — it supplements (and in narrative function somewhat replaces) Isaac's later blessing. "Double cave" = Cave of Machpelah (Gen 23).*
